title: TVS_iQube_FAQ
text: . 5. Range and Battery How do I get the most range? Avoid holding the brakes while riding, avoid hard acceleration and sustained top speed, and keep tyres at the recommended pressure. Distance to empty adapts to how you ride. The app can also show nearby charging stations. What battery does it use? Lithium-ion (NMC chemistry) in an aluminium casing with a battery management system that regulates temperature. The iQube S manual lists three packs at 52 V. There is no optional extra pack, and the battery cannot be removed by the owner. Tampering voids the warranty. How long does the battery last? TVS says it is designed to match the scooter's life. The FAQ gives a rough guide of 20-30% degradation by around 60,000-70,000 km. Replacement cost is not stated. Can I leave the scooter unused for a couple of months? Yes, but the battery self-discharges about

title: TVS_iQube_FAQ
text: Replacement cost is not stated. Can I leave the scooter unused for a couple of months? Yes, but the battery self-discharges about 5% every 10 days (roughly 15% a month). Leave it with at least 50% charge when parking for long. The manual says to charge to at least 30% once every 15 days. What about voltage fluctuations? The charger has built-in protection, but use a TVS-recommended charger and a properly earthed socket. Could the battery swell from overcharging? It is not designed to overcharge, and the protection system and battery health monitoring are meant to prevent that. 6. Service and Maintenance When is the first service due? At 6 months or 4,000 km, whichever comes first. After that, service every 4,000 km or 1 year, whichever is earlier. All services are paid.
